5331.idn: Name in the source: Bebot (title); printed äéàbóöt in the text; Nang-nda (cover name used by the language committee for the speech of six cantons); family in the source: langue du groupe Sara; famille Nilo-saharienne, branche chari-Nilotique…; the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: Le äéàbóöt est une langue à ton à l’instar des nombreuses langues africaines. Dans ces langues à ton, chaque syllabe est caractérisée par le ton. En d’autres termes, tout noyau syllabique est porteur de ton. ... Il se dégage de cette analyse que la langue äéàbóöt atteste trois tons ponctuels. Il s’agit du ton haut, moyen, et bas. D’après notre analyse, les tons haut et bas sont des tons sous-jacents c’est à dire des tons de la structure profonde de la langue. Par contre, le ton moyen provient de deux processus phonologiques.
tn.translation: Bebot is a tone language like many African languages. In these tone languages each syllable is characterised by tone; in other words, every syllable nucleus bears tone. ... It emerges from this analysis that Bebot attests three level tones: high, mid and low. According to our analysis, high and low are underlying tones, i.e. tones of the deep structure of the language. The mid tone, by contrast, comes from two phonological processes.
tn.cite: Madjirade, Yaphete. 2007. Approche de la phonologie lexicale du Bebot (langue du groupe Sara du Tchad). Mémoire de DEA en linguistique générale, Université de Yaoundé I, Département de Langues Africaines et Linguistique, dir. Beban Sammy Chumbow. x+217 pp.
tn.locator: ch. VI §6.0 p. 106 and ch. VII conclusion p. 161
tn.note: Three surface level tones H M L, every syllable; H and L underlying, M from Meeussen's rule (HH>HM) or default; contours derived; floating tones from deleted vowels. Name prints äéàbóöt.

5336.idn: Name in the source: dagba (la langue dagba); people: Dagba, part of the groupe Sara; family in the source: Grande famille Nilo-saharienne; Famille Chari-Nilotique; Branche Soudanais central; Sous-branche Sara-Bongo-Baguirmien; Groupe Sara; Langue Dagba (after Tucker in Barreteau 1978)

tn.quote: Le dagba est une langue à tons. Chaque syllabe est porteuse d’un ton et sert à des fins distinctives. Trois tons ponctuels sont identifiés en dagba: Le ton bas noté [`], le ton moyen [-] et le ton haut [´] La langue n’a pas à proprement de tons modulés. Mais ce que nous présentons comme tons modulés ne sont autres que la succession des tons ponctuels dans les dissyllabiques du type CVV ou CVVC. Ils sont au nombre de six dont trois montants et trois descendants.
tn.translation: Dagba is a tone language. Every syllable carries a tone, which serves distinctive purposes. Three level tones are identified in Dagba: the low tone written [`], the mid tone [-] and the high tone [´]. Strictly speaking the language has no contour tones. What we present as contour tones are nothing but successions of level tones in disyllabics of the type CVV or CVVC. There are six of them, three rising and three falling.
tn.cite: Yondorum, Charles. 2018. Phonologie et morphologie de la langue dagba [title page: Phonologie et morphologie du dagba]. Thèse présentée en vue de l'obtention du Doctorat/Ph.D en linguistique générale, Université de Yaoundé I, sous la direction de Philippe Mutaka Nguessimo, juin 2018. 348 pp. Deposited in DICAMES 2024, hdl:20.500.12177/11832.
tn.locator: p. 25, Première partie, Chapitre I 'Le tonème', Introduction; restated in Conclusion p. 239 and Tableau des tons ponctuels no1 p. 33-34
tn.note: Three level tones (L, M, H) on every syllable, set up by minimal pairs; six rising/falling contours = level sequences on CVV(C); French loans take HL; deverbal nouns by L->H; nothing on stress.

tn.quote: Surface forms in Fe’fe’ can carry any one of four discrete level tones, or a contour tone (either rising or falling). The solution in (49a) distinguishes only two underlying tone levels, though at the expense of positing an underlying rising tone.

tn.quote: Les oppositions tonales ci-dessus révèlent que les tons bas /B/, moyen /M/, mi-haut /H-/ et haut /H/ sont des tonèmes de la langue. Elles ont donc une fonction distinctive. ... Comme beaucoup de dialectes bété (kpɔkolo, gbadi, ɉibuo, guébié), le niabré atteste quatre tons ponctuels qui sont: Le ton haut ( ́ ), le ton mi-haut ( ̍ ), le ton moyen ( ̄ ) et le ton bas ( ̀ ). ... nous retenons que les tons modulés sur une même voyelle signifient qu’il s’agit d’une voyelle allongée. Et sur chaque voyelle figure un ton ponctuel.
tn.translation: The tonal oppositions above show that the low /B/, mid /M/, mid-high /H-/ and high /H/ tones are tonemes of the language. They thus have a distinctive function. ... Like many Bété dialects (kpɔkolo, gbadi, ɉibuo, guébié), Niabré attests four level tones: the high tone, the mid-high tone, the mid tone and the low tone. ... we retain that modulated tones on a single vowel mean that it is a lengthened vowel. And on each vowel there is a level tone.
tn.cite: Ouraga, Tété Mireille. 2025. Analyse phonologique des tons en niabré, parler bété de Gagnoa. Kurukan Fuga (Revue Africaine des Lettres, des Sciences Humaines et Sociales, Université des Lettres et des Sciences Humaines de Bamako) 4(14): 718-731.

Российская лингвистическая экспедиция в Кот-д'Ивуар и орфографические реформы в южных языках манде [Russian linguistic field trips to Cote d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. 5343.idn: Name in the source: гоо (Goo); family in the source: южные языки манде (South Mande group); closest relative тура (Tura); formerly considered a dialect intermediate between дан (Dan) and тура

tn.quote: Все эти языки политонические: половина из них (уан, муан, гуро, нген, бен) имеет по 3 уровневых тона (трехтоновый также и язык мано, распространенный в Гвинее и Либерии), половина (западный дан, кла-дан, гоо, тура, яурэ, гбан) — по 4; восточный дан имеет 5 уровневых тонов, при этом гуро, бен, западный и восточный дан, гбан имеют также модулированные тоны. Во всех этих языках тоны несут большую функциональную нагрузку и служат не только для лексического контраста, но и для выражения многочисленных грамматических значений.
tn.translation: All these languages are polytonic: half of them (Wan, Mwan, Guro, Ngen, Beng) have 3 level tones each (Mano, spoken in Guinea and Liberia, is also three-tone), half (Western Dan, Kla-Dan, Goo, Tura, Yaoure, Gban) have 4 each; Eastern Dan has 5 level tones, while Guro, Beng, Western and Eastern Dan and Gban also have modulated (contour) tones. In all these languages tones carry a heavy functional load and serve not only for lexical contrast but also to express numerous grammatical meanings.
tn.cite: Выдрин, В. Ф. [Vydrin, Valentin F.]. 2019. Российская лингвистическая экспедиция в Кот-д'Ивуар и орфографические реформы в южных языках манде [Russian linguistic field trips to Cote d'Ivoire and orthography reforms in the South Mande languages]. Кунсткамера (Kunstkamera) 2019, No. 4(6): 107-121.
tn.locator: p. 108, 'Введение'
tn.note: Survey: Goo has 4 level tones, no contour tones (not among languages listed with modulated tones), heavy lexical+grammatical load; labels not given (Aplonova 2019: extra-high, high, low, extra-low).

evidence_works.work: Lu 2018, Aspects of the grammar of Tunxi Hui: a transitional Sinitic language (PhD thesis, University of Hong Kong: pp. 47-56, 123-125)
evidence_works.detail: Reference grammar of Tunxi Hui, a second Hui variety beside the entry's Qimen. Data: recorded daily conversations between native speakers plus linguistic elicitation (p. 28), consultants native-born Tunxi District residents over fifty (p. 31). Ch. 2.5 Tones: 'Tunxi Hui has six citation tones and a very complex tone sandhi system' (p. 47); sandhi rule (i): 'it is exclusively the preceding tone in a disyllabic word or phrase that will change its tone value, a pattern known as right-dominant tone sandhi' (p. 49); 'Neutral tones in Tunxi Hui, while they may be found, are not as evident or as common as in Mandarin. They only occur in functional words' (p. 54). The word 'stress' occurs once in the thesis, in 5.1.1 on strong vs weak personal-pronoun forms: strong forms 'are prosodically prominent, in terms of not only volume and length, but also and pitch and timbre' (p. 123) and 'the unstressed weak forms are' ungrammatical in contrastive constructions (p. 125); this is phrasal strong/weak-form prominence of pronouns, not a word-stress rule. No statement on lexical stress or its absence.

tn.quote: Izere has 29 consonant phonemes, 7 vowel phonemes and 3 level tones. ... There are five tones in Izere, three level and two contour tones (LM & HL). Contour tones occur in loanwords, words with potentially onomatopoeic names such as those of birds and where a tonally dissimilar VV sequence has been shortened ... As such these synchronic occurrences are probably transitional and Izere can be regarded as having an underlying three-height system. Tones are marked as follows; HIGH acute accent above the syllable kú to die MID unmarked fa to count LOW grave accent over the syllable mì I ...

tn.note: Five tones: high, mid, low, rising (LM), falling (HL); contours only in loans, bird names, shortened VV, so underlyingly three heights per the authors. Affixes bear varied tones. Nothing on stress.

refs.ref: Ōtake Masami (大竹昌巳). 2024. 契丹語の音調 [Pitch Realization in Khitan]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu: Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 165: 85-110. DOI 10.11435/gengo.165.0_85

5351.loc: p. 105 (sec. 4.1) and p. 106 (sec. 4.2); English abstract p. 110 restates: 'Khitan was a phrase language with an L tone at the left edge and an H tone at the right edge of every word or phrase'
5351.idn: Name in the source: 契丹語 (Khitan); family in the source: マクロモンゴル語族 (Macro-Mongolic family); モンゴル諸語と系統関係を有する 'related to the Mongolic languages' but not their direct ancestor

tn.quote: したがってこのことは，遼代初期の契丹語が，初頭音節のピッチが低く，末音節のピッチが高いという一定の音調形式を有したことを意味していると解釈することができる。... モンゴル諸語は語彙声調（lexical tone）も語彙強勢（lexical stress）も持たないが，韻律語もしくはアクセント句（accentual phrase）等，後語彙的な韻律単位の境界で実現する句音調（phrasal tone）をもつ phrase language（Féry 2010, 2017: 269–281）に分類される言語であり，... 契丹語が現代モンゴル諸語のような phrase language であったことを物語っている。... 契丹語音訳語彙の陰陽調字の分布は，この言語が左端を L 音調で明示し，緩やかなピッチの上昇ののち右端を H 音調で明示するという，左右両端の 2 つの境界画定機能をもつ音調によって形づくられるピッチ曲線を有したことを示すと解釈できる。
tn.translation: This can therefore be interpreted to mean that early-Liao Khitan had a fixed pitch pattern in which the initial syllable was low-pitched and the final syllable high-pitched. ... The Mongolic languages have neither lexical tone nor lexical stress, but are classified as phrase languages (Féry 2010, 2017: 269-281) having phrasal tones realised at the boundaries of post-lexical prosodic units such as the prosodic word or accentual phrase, ... [this] tells us that Khitan was a phrase language like the modern Mongolic languages. ...
tn.cite: Ōtake Masami (大竹昌巳). 2024. 契丹語の音調 [Pitch Realization in Khitan]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu: Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 165: 85-110. DOI 10.11435/gengo.165.0_85
tn.locator: p. 105 (sec. 4.1) and p. 106 (sec. 4.2); English abstract p. 110 restates: 'Khitan was a phrase language with an L tone at the left edge and an H tone at the right edge of every word or phrase'
tn.note: Extinct Khitan reconstructed as a phrase language: no lexical tone; every word/phrase low at left edge (L boundary tone), high at right (H). Evidence: tone categories of Chinese transcription chars.

5351.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

5352.idn: Name in the source: коранко; западный и восточный коранко; санкаран-коранко (transitional idiom between Koranko and Maninka); family in the source: Язык коранко входит в группу моколе, при этом он является частью единого с манден далектного континуума (Mokole group; part of one dialect continuum with Manden)

tn.quote: Большинство идиомов манден имеет две базовые тоновые схемы слов. Так, в манинка-мори выделяются слова с высоким и с низким (восходящим) тоном. Тоновые схемы односложных и многосложных слов совпадают. Тоны могут реализоваться как на одной гласной (bá ‛мать’, bà ‛коза’), так и на двух и более: bóló ‛рука’, mòsò ‛женщина’. ... 1. Манинка. Основные признаки: неинвертированные тоновые схемы ... 2. Конья ... Основные признаки: инвертированные тоновые схемы ... 3. Коранко. Фонологически ближе к манинка, чем к конья, однако имеет большое количество лексических расхождений как одним, так и с другим.
tn.translation: Most Manden idioms have two basic tonal word patterns. Thus in Maninka-Mori words with high and with low (rising) tone are distinguished. The tonal patterns of monosyllabic and polysyllabic words coincide. The tones may be realised on one vowel (bá 'mother', bà 'goat') or on two or more: bóló 'arm', mòsò 'woman'. ... 1. Maninka. Main features: non-inverted tonal patterns ... 2. Konya ... Main features: inverted tonal patterns ... 3. Koranko. Phonologically closer to Maninka than to Konya, but with many lexical divergences from both.
tn.cite: Давыдов, А. В. [Davydov, Artem V.]. 2017. Манден диалекты Гвинеи [Manden dialects of Guinea]. In В. Ф. Выдрин, Ю. В. Мазурова, А. А. Кибрик & Е. Б. Маркус (eds.), Языки мира: Языки манде, 164-171. Санкт-Петербург: Нестор-История.
tn.locator: p. 170, sec. 6 (tone paragraph); then p. 166, sec. 5 items 1-3
tn.note: Two word-level tone classes (high vs low, low realised as rising) stated for Manden idioms generally; Koranko sides with the non-inverted Maninka type; ~70 tone-marked Koranko forms; no stress/TBU.

5352.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 7 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

refs.ref: Kuku, Nabil Abdalla. 2012. Laru Vowel Harmony. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 10: 17-34. Juba: SIL.

5353.idn: Name in the source: Laru; Liira or Alliira (names given by outsiders); dialects Yilaru, Yidundili, Yogoromany (description is on Yilaru, the central dialect); family in the source: Niger-Kordofanian language, in the Heiban group (with Moro, Otoro, Kwalib, Tira, Hadra, Shoai)

tn.quote: 4. Tone There are two level tones (High and Low) and two contour tones (High-Low and Low-High). (3) H dúŋə́ 'snake' HL lây 'liver' L dùŋə̀ 'soot' LH lə̌y 'eye' At most, two tones may be assigned to any one vowel of one and two syllable words. Only one tone may be assigned per vowel in words of three syllables or longer, such as dɔ̀ŋɔ̀rɔ́ 'lizard' and lə̀blə́ⁿdí 'rifle'. Grammatical tone is present, but more study is needed to provide an authoritative statement.
tn.cite: Kuku, Nabil Abdalla. 2012. Laru Vowel Harmony. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 10: 17-34. Juba: SIL.
tn.locator: Section 4 'Tone', p. 21
tn.note: Two level tones (H, L) plus two contours (HL, LH); contours only in 1-2-syllable words and treated as two tones on one vowel; grammatical tone present but unanalysed; nothing on stress.

5354.idn: Name in the source: Limbum (Central/Warr dialect); family in the source: Grassfields Bantu language

tn.quote: In previous work (Fiore 1987; Fransen 1995), Limbum has been described as a tone language with three level tones (H, L, M) and four contour tones (HL, LM, ML, LL). ... (following Fiore 1987 and Fransen 1995, we assume that the syllable is the TBU in Limbum). ... there are three classes of tones in Limbum: level tones which remain level tones in all positions (L, M, H), level tones that alternate with falling contour tones at the end of declarative sentences and wh-questions (L(L), M(L), H(L)), and a rising contour tone (LM).
tn.cite: Gjersøe, Siri, Jude Nformi & Ludger Paschen. 2019. Hybrid falling tones in Limbum. In Emily Clem, Peter Jenks & Hannah Sande (eds.), Theory and description in African Linguistics: Selected papers from the 47th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 95-118. Berlin: Language Science Press.
tn.locator: pp. 95-96 (section 1), p. 103 (section 3.1.1), p. 107 (section 3.2)
tn.note: 7 tones (H M L; falling HL ML LL; rising LM; HM marginal, fn.1); contours = two tonal root nodes on one syllable, falling ones surface only phrase-finally via floating L%; downstep only generic.
